# Feature: Unified Browser Fill Engine

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-011
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)
**Predecessors**: FEAT-FP-009 (`feature_browser_widget_observability.md`) and FEAT-FP-010
(`feature_browser_widget_drivers.md`) — both implemented. This feature **supersedes the tool
surface** those features produced while keeping their driver internals: the observation
enrichment, the weekday cross-check, the pattern-based drivers, and the verify-committed rule
all survive; the four-tool fill surface does not.

Collapse the model-visible fill surface to **two tools** — `browser_fill_form` and
`browser_fill_element` — and move _everything_ about operating a control into one deterministic
engine in `packages/core`: element discovery, widget-type dispatch, suggestion dropdowns, date
calendars and date inputs, radio/checkbox/select handling, retries, stale-ref recovery, and —
new — **dismissing the widget so the page is left actionable**. The same engine drives saved
workflow replay through a new semantic `fill_element` step, so a promoted workflow with
`check_in`/`check_out` params can actually change the dates.

### Evidence from run `20260808T042317Z-do-6bcdac53`

Goal: cheap hotels near Frisco TX, Sep 6–12 2026, on Expedia. 42 tool calls, 328s, $0.17 —
and the brief concedes: _"Specific dated pricing could not be retrieved because the Expedia
calendar widget persisted as a modal overlay that blocked the Search button."_ The trace shows
the agent ran the identical navigate → fill destination → pick suggestion → pick dates
sequence **four times** without ever reaching a dated results page.

| #   | Fault                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A   | Drivers commit but never dismiss. `restore()` only closes a widget that was _closed on entry_; Expedia auto-opens the calendar, so `wasOpen: true` left the modal up, blocking the Search button                             | `open-state.ts` `restore`; trace repeats the full form sequence 4×; brief's own failure note                                                                                                  |
| B   | The model is punished for the driver's re-renders: refs from the pre-pick observation go stale, and no model-facing tool heals them                                                                                          | 3× `STALE_ELEMENT_REF` (seq 9, 31, 57), each immediately after a successful widget drive                                                                                                      |
| C   | Calendar reads that find nothing report nothing: `displayedMonths: []`, "target month is not represented safely"                                                                                                             | 2× `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` (seq 29, 55); `directionFor` returns null on an empty read; trace shows a probable open/close double-toggle (two consecutive clicks on the same Dates trigger) |
| D   | Detection-before-acting misses widgets that reveal themselves only after typing: the destination committed via the **plain-text** driver and the suggestion dropdown was never engaged                                       | seq 29 `details.applied`: `{"field":"Where to?","driver":"plain-text","committed":"Frisco, Texas"}`                                                                                           |
| E   | Promoted traces are date-brittle by construction: day cells recorded as `role: button, name: "Sunday, September 6, 2026"` plus absolute XPaths; the replay executor has no widget awareness and no semantic step verb exists | `trace.json` steps; `workflow-to-plan.ts` verb union; `executor/step-handlers/` has only primitive `fill`/`click`                                                                             |

**Targets**:

- The Expedia goal completes with a dated results page in **≤15 tool calls**, with zero
  `STALE_ELEMENT_REF` and zero dismiss/overlay failures.
- Google's hotel-finder date **inputs** (not buttons) fill correctly through the same tool with
  no site-specific code.
- A `do --save-as` workflow of the Expedia flow replays LLM-free with _different_ dates supplied
  as params.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules (coding standards, architecture, testing, logging, security) are in
> `.spec-lite/memory.md` and are unchanged by this feature.

### Approach

**The value's shape carries the intent; the engine owns the strategy.** The model states
_field + value_, nothing else: `"2026-09-06"` is a date, `"2026-09-06..2026-09-12"` a range,
`"checked"`/`"unchecked"` a toggle (only when the resolved control is actually a
checkbox/radio/switch — otherwise it is text), anything else is text-or-option. There is no
driver name, no `pick_suggestion` flag, no family parameter anywhere in the model's vocabulary.
FEAT-FP-010's registry/family/detection machinery becomes an internal implementation detail of
one engine entry point.

**React, don't just pre-detect.** FEAT-FP-010 dispatched on a _closed-state_ detection score,
which is exactly how fault D happened. The engine keeps cheap pre-detection for controls that
declare themselves (`<select>`, `<input type="date">`, calendar triggers with committed date
values) but adds a mandatory **post-act reaction step** on every text-like fill: watch
(bounded poll) for a floating container that appears after typing; if candidates show up,
rank them against the typed text and select the unique best; a tie is a typed failure, and
no-tier-match keeps the typed literal and dismisses the popup. A dropdown the site only
renders after the third keystroke is handled identically to one detection predicted.

**Commit-and-release is part of fill semantics.** After the committed value verifies, the
engine dismisses whatever floating container is associated with the field — _regardless of who
opened it_: click an unambiguous in-container commit control (`Done`/`Apply`/`OK`/`Save`/
`Close`), else press `Escape`, then **re-verify the committed value survived dismissal** (some
widgets revert on Escape — if it reverted, reopen and retry via commit control only) and verify
the container is actually hidden. A fill that leaves a modal blocking the page returns
`WIDGET_DISMISS_FAILED`, never a silent success. `restore()`'s leave-it-how-you-found-it rule
is retired: in `browser_fill_form`, field N+1's drive simply re-opens what it needs.
Deterministic beats stateful.

**Stale refs heal in the controller, for every caller.** `AgentBrowserController` already
mints refs from an identity key (`refIdByIdentity`); it now also remembers each ref's identity
record. Any ref-taking action (`click`, `fill`, `evaluateOn`) that hits a stale ref internally
re-scans (uncapped, digest-untracked), re-resolves the identity `(role, name, group)` to a
unique live element, swaps the ref, and retries **once**. `STALE_ELEMENT_REF` surfaces only
when the identity is gone or ambiguous. The engine keeps one _stronger_ second line for its own
target only: re-acquisition by the caller's `field` string, because a trigger's accessible name
embeds its value and _changes_ as the widget commits (`"Dates, Fri, Aug 21 …"` →
`"Dates, Sun, Sep 6 …"`) — identity healing alone cannot survive that. The bespoke
`tracedWidgetPort` healing wrapper collapses into these two layers.

**Failures must say what the engine saw.** The calendar reader gains non-`<table>` grid
coverage (div-based `[role="grid"]`/`[role="row"]` structures, aria-label-dated cells) and its
failure payloads name what was actually found — container resolved or not, cell count, months
parsed — so `displayedMonths: []` with no explanation cannot recur. The weekday cross-check,
the never-guess ambiguity rule, and the verify-committed rule are unchanged; they are the
parts of FEAT-FP-010 that worked.

**Replay drives the same engine.** A new additive workflow verb `fill_element` carries the
field's semantic identity (accessible name + ranked locator chain fallback) and a value
_expression_ (literal, `{{param:…}}`, `{{secret:…}}`, `{{capture:…}}`). The trace records one
semantic `fill_element` step per field instead of N primitive clicks with baked-in dates;
promotion maps it 1:1; a new executor step handler builds a `WidgetPort` over the replay page
and calls the same `fillField`. The engine is deterministic, so zero-LLM replay is preserved
by construction. A form is consecutive `fill_element` steps — no `fill_form` verb is added to
the YAML schema. Existing saved workflows with primitive steps parse, lint, and replay exactly
as today (additive union change only).

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **Model-visible tool names follow the noun-last convention the user set**: `browser_fill_form`
  and `browser_fill_element` (note: _not_ the existing `browser_form_fill` spelling). The
  catalog hash changes; that is expected and recorded in the manifest per run.
- **No system-prompt change, no `PROMPT_VERSION` bump.** Guidance moves via tool descriptions
  and the `do` profile addendum only, as FEAT-FP-010 established. `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` stays
  `agent-v7`.
- **Workflow YAML compatibility is additive-only** (memory §General): the `fill_element` verb is
  a new union member; no existing verb, field, or lint behavior changes for saved workflows.
- **`packages/core` gains a new `fill/` module and must not import `@yantra/agent`** — the
  `WidgetPort` seam from FEAT-FP-010 remains the boundary; the executor implements the same
  port for replay.
- No other overrides — see memory.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No persistent schema changes beyond the additive workflow verb. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does
not exist and none is introduced.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`FillIntent`** (`core/src/fill/intent.ts`) — discriminated union, derived from value shape × resolved control kind:
  - `{ kind: 'text', text: string }` — free text (also the fallback when `checked`/`unchecked` targets a non-toggle)
  - `{ kind: 'option', value: string }` — choose from offered choices (select, listbox, radio group, typeahead suggestion)
  - `{ kind: 'date', date: string }` — ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, calendar-validity checked
  - `{ kind: 'date_range', from: string, to: string }` — from `"<from>..<to>"`, `from ≤ to` enforced
  - `{ kind: 'toggle', checked: boolean }` — from `"checked"`/`"unchecked"` on checkbox/radio/switch roles
  - `{ kind: 'secret', key: string }` — `browser_fill_element` only; never enters `fill_form`

- **`FieldIdentity`** (`core/src/fill/types.ts`) — how the engine (re)acquires its target:
  - `field` (string) — the caller's name-or-ref string; the durable identity
  - `target` (`WidgetTarget`) — ref/role/name/group/value as first resolved

- **`FillOutcome`** — discriminated union:
  - `{ ok: true, driver: string, committed: string, actions: number, dismissed: boolean }` —
    `dismissed` is true when a floating container was closed as part of commit-and-release
  - `{ ok: false, errorCode: FillErrorCode, message, retryable, details }` — `details` always
    names observed state (see constraint below)

- **`FillErrorCode`** — closed union; FEAT-FP-010's `WIDGET_*` codes minus `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED`
  (unrecognized now falls through to plain text), plus:
  - `WIDGET_DISMISS_FAILED` — value committed but an overlay could not be closed; `details.stillOpen`
    names the container, `details.committed` the value (retryable)
  - `FILL_VALUE_INVALID` — malformed date, impossible range, or secret-shaped literal; refused
    before any page interaction (retryable)
  - `WIDGET_ELEMENT_REPLACED` — kept from FEAT-FP-010, now emitted only after _both_ healing
    layers fail

- **Calendar diagnostic contract** — every calendar failure's `details` must include:
  `{ containerResolved: boolean, cellsSeen: number, monthsParsed: string[], displayedMonths: string[] }`

- **`AgentTraceStep`** (`agent/src/runtime/trace.ts`) — new member:
  - `{ kind: 'fill_element', host, field: { name: string, role: string, group: string | null },
locator: LocatorCandidate[], value: TraceFillValue, requires_confirmation: boolean }` —
    one per field; the engine's internal clicks/fills no longer append primitive trace steps

- **`WorkflowStep`** (`protocol/src/schemas/workflow.ts`) — new union member:
  - `{ verb: 'fill_element', locator: string, field_name: string,
value: WorkflowValueExpression, requires_confirmation?: boolean, … }` — `locator` names a
    `_locators` chain (fallback resolution), `field_name` is the accessible-name identity the
    engine resolves first; added to `CONFIRMABLE_WORKFLOW_VERBS`

- **`Step`** (`protocol/src/schemas/steps.ts`) — matching `fill_element` plan step with
  `value: ValueRef` (literal | param | secret | capture)

### Relationships

- One `browser_fill_form` call → N `FieldIdentity`/`FillIntent` pairs → N `fill_element` trace
  steps, applied in order, stopping at first failure with prior `applied` reported.
- One workflow `fill_element` step → one engine `fillField` call at replay.
- `AgentBrowserController` and the executor's replay page adapter both implement `WidgetPort`.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `AgentBrowserController` gains `identityByRef: Map<string, {role, name, group}>`, populated at
  ref mint, cleared with `refs`/`refIdByIdentity` on navigation commit and teardown.
- Reaction poll: `REACTION_WAIT_MS = 1500` at 150ms. Dismissal commit-control pattern:
  `/^(done|apply|ok|save|close)$/i`, single enabled match required. All existing `WidgetBudget`
  bounds (`maxPagingSteps` 12, `maxActions` 24, absolute deadline) unchanged.
- Healing retries: exactly **one** identity re-resolution per action, one field-string
  re-acquisition per engine drive — no unbounded loops.

### TASK-001: Fill engine entry point, intent parsing, and commit-and-release

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `fill/intent.ts`: `parseFillValue(raw, controlKind) → FillIntent | FillErrorCode`.
    Shape rules from §3; `2026-02-31` and reversed ranges are `FILL_VALUE_INVALID` with the
    expected format named; `checked`/`unchecked` maps to `toggle` only for
    checkbox/radio/switch roles, else falls through to `text`.
  - Create `fill/engine.ts` `fillField(port, identity, intent, budget)`: resolve target →
    dispatch: `select` → native-select driver; `toggle` → click-if-needed + `checked` verify;
    `date`/`date_range` → date-input driver when the control is an input with a date format
    (Google hotel finder shape), else calendar driver; `text`/`option` → fill then the TASK-002
    reaction step. Always end with `readCommitted` + `matchesIntent`, then the dismissal pass.
  - Create `fill/dismiss.ts`: resolve the field's floating container (`resolveContainer`,
    `allowUnlinked`); if open → click a single enabled in-container control matching
    `/^(done|apply|ok|save|close)$/i`, else `press('Escape')`; verify hidden; re-read committed
    and, on revert, reopen and retry via commit control only; still open/reverted →
    `WIDGET_DISMISS_FAILED` with `details.stillOpen` and `details.committed`.
  - Retire `restore()` in `open-state.ts`; drivers no longer close anything themselves.
  - `registry.ts` stops being exported from the core barrel; `fillField` is the only public
    entry. Export the `fill/` barrel from `core/src/index.ts`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Intent: each shape maps correctly; `checked` on a textbox is text; `2026-02-31`, `b..a`,
    and `2026-13-01..2026-13-02` are `FILL_VALUE_INVALID` with no page interaction.
  - A committed date range whose calendar stays open gets dismissed via a `Done` button; via
    `Escape` when no button exists; `dismissed: true` reported in both cases.
  - An Escape that reverts the committed value → reopen + commit-control path, verified by the
    final committed read.
  - No commit control, Escape ineffective, container still visible → `WIDGET_DISMISS_FAILED`
    naming the container; the committed value is still reported in details.
  - A field with no floating container (plain input) skips dismissal entirely (`dismissed: false`).
  - The fault-A regression: a widget that was **already open on entry** is still dismissed
    after commit — the run's exact failure.

### TASK-002: Reactive suggestion handling replaces pre-detection-only dispatch

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `fill/react.ts` `watchAndSelect(port, identity, typedText, budget)`: after a
    text-like fill, poll up to `REACTION_WAIT_MS = 1500` at 150ms for a floating container that
    became visible after typing (aria-controls/owns link, sibling popup, or DOM diff — reuse
    `resolveContainer` machinery). Collect candidates via `candidates.ts` (no `role="option"`
    requirement, per FEAT-FP-010). Rank against `typedText`: unique best → click + verify
    committed; tie → `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` with `details.offered`; candidates present but
    none match any tier → dismiss the popup, keep the typed literal, succeed as text.
  - `text` and `option` intents both route through this: a plain input that never pops a
    container commits as typed text; a typeahead commits the selected suggestion.
  - Delete the standalone typeahead pre-detection path in the engine dispatch (the driver's
    candidate logic is reused; its closed-state `detect` is no longer load-bearing).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - The fault-D regression: a textbox whose suggestion list (`role="button"` children) renders
    600ms **after** typing gets its best suggestion committed — with no pre-detection signal on
    the closed field.
  - No popup appears → typed literal committed, zero extra clicks, no wait beyond the poll bound.
  - Two same-tier candidates → `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE`, no click dispatched.
  - Candidates that match no tier → popup dismissed, literal kept, `ok: true` as text.
  - Suggestions arriving at 1.2s are still selected (async poll, not a single read).

### TASK-005: `browser_fill_element` tool (absorbs the secret path); retire `browser_fill`

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - New tool `browser_fill_element`. Params: `field` (visible name or `eNN` ref) and `value` —
    reuse `browser_fill`'s proven union (plain string first for small-model ergonomics, tagged
    `literal`, tagged `secret_ref`). `sanitizationProfile: 'authenticated'`, `mutating: true`;
    `requiresConfirmation` for secret_ref, exactly as `browser_fill` today.
  - Literal path: `SECRET_SHAPE` guard → `parseFillValue` → `fillField`. Secret path: existing
    `assertHostBinding` → `resolver.resolve` → `withSecret(value, …)` machinery moves over
    verbatim, driving the engine's plain-text commit (secrets never enter react/option
    selection and are never read back — the committed verify is skipped for secret fills, and
    password fields remain unread per FEAT-FP-009's in-page withholding).
  - Success returns `{ committed, driver, dismissed, observation }` (committed omitted on

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: `browser_fill_element` with `secret_ref` is the sole credentialed path, inheriting
  `browser_fill`'s host-binding, consent confirmation, `withSecret` scoping, and trace-records-
  key-only behavior verbatim. `browser_fill_form` is literals-only by schema. Secrets never
  enter suggestion ranking, committed-value reads, or dismissal re-verification; password/OTP
  fields remain unread in-page (FEAT-FP-009). Workflow `fill_element` secret values resolve at
  the executor boundary with the same host binding.
- **Error Handling**: `FillErrorCode` is a closed union; every failure carries `retryable` and
  observed-state details (the calendar diagnostic contract is mandatory). All waits and retries
  are bounded: one identity heal per action, one field re-acquisition per drive, reaction poll
  1500ms, paging 12, actions 24, absolute deadline. `trackFailureStreak` still keys
  `${tool}:${errorCode}` for stuck-loop breaking.
- **Logging**: no new log statements carry field values. Trace `fill_element` values are masked
  (`userInput.mask`) or secret keys; `tool-calls.jsonl` continues to receive only the sanitized
  model projection. The dismissal pass adds no value-bearing logs.
- **Security**: net posture unchanged or stronger. The tool-surface shrink removes two
  `mutating: true` entry points; verify-committed and never-guess rules are retained; page
  mutation remains limited to the FEAT-FP-010 tagging fallback with guaranteed cleanup; URL
  provenance, ethics, robots, and rate-limit paths untouched. Workflow YAML change is additive;
  saved workflows and run artifacts remain compatible (memory §General).
